title: Importance of Performing Obligatory Prayers
summary: Performing obligatory prayers is crucial, and missing them intentionally is a major sin.
translation: It is imperative for every accountable Muslim man or woman to perform prayers. Until a person performs the prayer, it remains their obligation, and scholars agree that intentionally missing an obligatory prayer is a major sin. In Islam, just as adultery, theft, and alcohol consumption are major sins, similarly, intentionally missing a prayer is a major sin. Some have even said it is greater than those sins to intentionally abandon a prayer. Therefore, every Muslim should ensure they perform each prayer on time, and if a prayer is missed, they should perform it at the earliest opportunity. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that if someone forgets a prayer, they should perform it as soon as they remember. In another hadith, it is stated that if someone forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, the expiation is to perform it when they remember. This hadith is in Sahih Bukhari and Muslim, and Tirmidhi mentions that the Prophet (peace be upon him) instructed if someone forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, they should perform it when they remember. However, it's crucial to note that purposely forming a habit of missing or delaying a prayer is mentioned in the noble hadith as a grave sin, and even a major sin; thus, one should not intentionally miss a prayer. In terms of making up for missed prayers during one's lifetime, they should be performed with the intention of 'Qada-e-Umri,' and one should pray to Allah to make it easy. The way to perform these missed lifetime prayers is just as we perform regular prayers, but it's important to understand the intention for Qada prayers when knowing specifically which prayer is missed. For instance, specifying the prayer as 'I am performing the make-up (Qada) prayer for the Fajr prayer from last Friday.' However, if the specific day or time of the missed prayer isn't known, one can intend as such: for example, 'I am performing the first Fajr prayer from those that I missed,' or 'I am performing the first Dhuhr prayer from those that I missed.' In this way, you can intend similarly for other prayers. The advantage of this is that the first Qada prayer in your lifetime will be performed, and as you perform more, the remaining ones can be intended likewise. Therefore, you will make the intention like 'I am performing the first Fajr prayer among those I have missed.' The method is quite easy if one makes an intention. When there are five times in a day, one can attempt to perform the missed obligatory prayers with these. If unable, at least attempt to perform one prayer a day. Otherwise, a person can perform as many as desired, like a hundred or two hundred prayers a day depending on available time. Effort and prayer are essential; Allah will certainly ease it for those who make the effort. The expiation for any missed prayer during life is to perform it; there is no other expiation. If someone was sick and passed away in that sickness, that's another matter regarding giving fidya, but if fidya was not given or willed, they will be questioned about the missed prayer because it was neither performed nor intended to perform.
